newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM predicts long battle for hostage release.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM predicts long battle for hostage release.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Thursday it could be a long time before hundreds of hostages held by leftist guerrillas in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima are released.
"This is going to be a prolonged battle," Hashimoto told reporters. He did not elaborate.

The rebels called on Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori to personally negotiate for the release of the captives, including two Peruvian ministers and at least 15 ambassadors from Asia, Europe and the Americas.
Fujimori, who suspended all public activities and called an emergency cabinet meeting for Thursday morning, has so far not commented publicly on the attack.
However, in a conversation with Hashimoto, the president said Interior Minister Juan Briones Davila was handling negotiations.
While estimates by the government and released hostages put the number of captives between 200 and 300, a letter signed by the captives and faxed to relatives said the rebels were holding 490 people.
The Cuban-inspired Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels said they would kill the hostages unless the government freed up to 500 jailed comrades.
Guerrilla spokesmen said they had targeted the Japanese ambassador's home in protest at Tokyo's support for President Fujimori, the son of Japanese immigrants, and his economic policies.
Japan was chosen as a target "due to the constant meddling of the Japanese government in Peru", one rebel spokesman said.
